fields.why: The article says 'no significant differences', but it reports no p-values, no CIs and no testing method; it names only the software (SPSS). Under v5 that 'significant' does not imply an unnamed test, so no procedure is recorded.
Same reason: under v5 a 'significant' with no p-values, CIs or testing method anywhere in the article is not a test.
No CIs are reported and no test is recordable under the v5 rule on 'significantly' with no test, so inference is none. A correctly flags this in view_issues.
Bidi-use percentages for 4 race/ethnicity groups and 6 grades are only set side by side in Table 1; with no recordable test, 'omnibus test' is not supported.

brief_issues: Only record A was provided, so B's justification was not rated. The v5 rule calls such a 'significant' colloquial, yet here it is plainly a statistical claim with no reported test; the rule still decides the case.
